item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"The old syntaxin entries 1br0 and 1ez3 should not be read as defining independent syntaxin folds or full syntaxin N-terminal domains. They are partial N-terminal-domain observations: short helical pieces of the same larger Habc regulatory domain whose complete three-helix bundle is seen in syntaxin 1A from 1dn1 chain B. SCOPe’s current treatment therefore makes 1dn1B the biologically interpretable full-domain representative, while 1br0 and 1ez3 are fragment-level representatives of that domain context.\n\nThe practical consequence is to weaken, not strengthen, inference from the fragments. A match to 1br0 or 1ez3 is evidence for local helical similarity to part of a syntaxin N-terminal domain; by itself it is not enough to assign the whole Habc fold, the full syntaxin N-terminal family, or syntaxin-specific regulatory function. Homology and template transfer should be made at the domain level using the full syntaxin N-terminal domain, exemplified by 1dn1 chain B, and fragment hits should be used only as supporting evidence after checking that their residues map consistently onto the complete domain architecture.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
